scenes.say: Twenty-two cars, three sessions and only ten spots in the final. How does qualifying work?
The first part lasts eighteen minutes. The six slowest drivers start seventeenth or lower.
In the second part all times are wiped, and another six drop out in fifteen minutes.
In the final part the top ten have twelve minutes to fight for pole.
The track gets quicker every minute, so everyone waits until the end. And anyone far too slow risks missing the race.
Follow qualifying lap by lap, live on LapRadar.

title: Qualifying Q1, Q2, Q3: how 22 cars become one pole
